why_how.text: A governor-declared state of emergency automatically cancels road tests, with a regional declaration canceling tests only in the affected region.
An examiner may cancel a road test because of unsafe weather, and an applicant whose test is canceled for that reason may reschedule without an added fee.
Failing, arriving unprepared, having an unacceptable vehicle, lacking a qualified sponsor, missing or arriving late for a road test can each cause the road-test fee to be charged.
Canceling or rescheduling a road test with less than seventy-two hours of notice causes the road-test fee to be charged.
An examiner may reject a road test when the applicant or sponsor shows signs of impairment by alcohol or another substance.
An examiner may reject a road test when alcohol or cannabis odor comes from the applicant, sponsor, their clothes or the vehicle.
Children, babies or animals that cannot be left supervised can cause road-test rejection, although trained service animals are allowed and emotional-support animals are not.
Applicants should arrive about fifteen minutes before their road-test appointment.
Specialized features such as cameras or parking assistance need not be disabled for a road test, but the applicant’s driving ability without sole reliance on them is still tested.
Necessary adaptive equipment or a need to use specialized features results in a mechanical or software aid restriction on the license.
The applicant, examiner and sponsor are the usual road-test occupants, with a language interpreter also permitted when allowed.
Road-test occupants may include a trained service animal, but not children, pets or emotional-support animals.
The applicant and sponsor or interpreter may converse during the road test only with the examiner’s authorization.
A deaf or hard-of-hearing applicant can request a road test with an interpreter through the RMV’s accommodation process.
Before a deaf or hard-of-hearing applicant’s test, the examiner explains communication and test elements, and written test information is supplied for review with the interpreter.
A road-test applicant with a question may pull over when safe and communicate with the examiner.
The RMV applies zero tolerance to violent or abusive conduct by road-test applicants and sponsors.

Every Class D road-test applicant needs a sponsor, including an applicant who has a valid foreign driver license.
A Class D sponsor must be at least twenty-one, have at least a year of driving experience and hold a valid license issued by their home state.
A person holding a foreign driver license cannot serve as a road-test sponsor.
Without RMV Road Test Program approval, one operator cannot sponsor more than three different applicants in a year.

why_how.text: The examiner cancels a road test if the vehicle is considered unsafe, and the applicant must show its registration and have it properly inspected.
The test vehicle needs a seat beside the driver for the examiner and a rear seat behind the driver for the sponsor.
A sponsor cannot ride in the bed of a two-passenger pickup during the road test.
The test vehicle’s parking brake must be accessible to the examiner for an emergency stop, whether it uses a manual control or an electric button.
The examiner decides whether the parking brake is accessible, and a centrally placed parking brake helps avoid an access problem.
No fee is charged for a scheduled road test prevented solely because the examiner cannot access the braking system.
Driving-instruction vehicles need a second foot brake for the instructor or examiner and the required signage.
A road test cannot proceed when the vehicle’s parking brake fails the legally required test.
A vehicle can be rejected when its parking brake is too far from the examiner to reach easily during an emergency.

For an out-of-state-registered test vehicle, proof must show Massachusetts minimum insurance limits of twenty-five thousand and fifty thousand dollars for bodily injury and thirty thousand dollars for property damage.
An insurance policy or certificate stating the coverage limits may serve as proof of test-vehicle insurance.
A rented test vehicle requires the rental agreement and a rental-company letter on company letterhead authorizing both applicant and sponsor to use it for the road test.
The rental authorization documents are not required for a leased test vehicle.
A vehicle fitted with a limited-use donut spare tire cannot be used for the road test.
A dealer-plated passenger vehicle is acceptable for a road test only when the examiner is satisfied that the applicant is the dealer, the dealer’s spouse or a dealership salesperson.

An acceptable farm-plated road-test vehicle requires proof that the applicant is the farmer’s family member or employee and must be a suitable nonpassenger vehicle, such as a pickup with a sponsor’s rear seat.
A vehicle displaying a repair plate cannot be used for a road test.
